parakeet: When all else fails, apologetics retreat to the ultimate defensive perimeter. God is transcendent and therefore not subject to empirical investigation. But once again, we have to ask, how can an attribute be affirmed before the entity itself has been confirmed? Saying God is transcendent isn't a neutral observation. It's a massive, highly specific claim about the fundamental nature of God's existence. So the question immediately becomes, by what reliable method did you determine that God is transcendent? If the answer is scripture, tradition, theology, or faith, you're still reading from the internal script of the belief system. You can't use transcendence to explain why God can't be verified unless you've already verified enough about God to know that transcendence applies to him in the first place. Otherwise, transcendence isn't an explanation for why God can't be investigated. It's simply the claim being protected from the investigation. It's a verbal smoke bomb thrown to cover an exit. This exposes a glaring, irreconcilable contradiction at the heart of modern apologetics. When they want to argue for God, God is close, he's intimate, he's the immediate necessary explanation for the origin of the universe, the complexity of DNA, the structure of physics, and the fine-tuning of nature. He leaves footprints everywhere. But when a skeptic asks for evidence, God is suddenly pushed outside the universe. He's beyond measurement, beyond investigation, beyond comprehension, and completely outside the bounds of human logic. You don't get to have it both ways. You can't drag God into the physical sandbox to claim credit for creation and then sprint into the hyperdimensional clouds the moment we ask to look at his hands.
